prep.video2:
Video 1 - Game Developer Mindset - Overcoming the Obstacles
\\Game Development, needing the proper mindset (open) - Creativity + Innovation. 
---Maintaining a positive mindset and attitude to think inside and outside the box.
---Perseverance to keep eyes on the main goal, long journey ahead.

**Enjoying the Development Process
Customer Focus (target audience) - |Key to Success|
Needs of fans/users above everything

---Learn from failures, don't be discouraged, analyze them and move forward (grow)

---Be able to receive feedback/constructive criticism

>Don't be afraid to try new things
\\Practice as to refine new and old skills

>Technical Challenges - bugs, hardware issues, code structure
\\Strong team with diverse technical skills + testing protocol
---Record keeping to aid in troubleshooting when stuck

What type of character from mixamo is worth importing or taking inspiration from?

prepBoard.notes:
Seems fairly self explanatory:
Game Development is in the center with all the surrounding pieces. 

Most important part  that was not included was that it is meant to be fun. If you begin losing the passion and drive, take a step away.

pitch.understand:
Well the finish line is a completed game containing a story and certain components that are beloved by the team of creators.

>As for the work, it is a lengthy process. 
-First, attaining the proper mindset to grow and develop. 
-Other more logistical components are to keep a master document that can be referenced by all of the team so everyone is in line with the project and its deadlines/tasks. Proper file storage and record keeping.
-It will take facing challenges and overcoming them, learning from failure, to push through to the other side. 
-The coding part can be delegated to others, including AI. The truly difficult part is creating a story in which you are the #1 fan.
pitch.offer:
My contributions to a team, at first glance, are more conceptual and connective. 
-Others are more skilled with the technology, but I believe my ideas are sharp and quite helpful in the overall collaboration and story building. In the previous class, I was the main transcriber on the whiteboard of all the brainstorming we did. 

Anyone can work with the tech: that can be delegated like I have said. But being able to do the physical world things with a team is what make me valuable to a team. Keeping us in line and in the scope of where our story lies. Uplifting others to share ideas, whether they are appropriate in that moment or not. Team collaboration and proper communication to straighten our path to discovering the story within.
pitch.limits:
As mentioned, the technical aspects can be improved. I am familiar with AI usage, but in regards to getting it to code for me, my knowledge is fairly rudimentary. 
Aside from that, attaining that growth and developer mindset is still needing improvement. Facing the challenges, learning from mistakes, getting comfortable with being uncomfortable.

huddle.mission:
A 2-D wave-based game with escalating difficulty as the rounds progress. Online/offline, up to 4 players total.
The main goal is to see how far you can get until the enemies overwhelm you and defeat you.
huddle.framework: P2P can be advantageous in the development by guiding us to the end point of where our team wants the game to stand. There is not much of a story to derive from this type of game, as opposed to other single-player, story mode games, but an underlying story to the characters can help immersify the fans.

dayBReview.recap:
My job is to lead the team and direct us to where we are going (no goal in mind)
\\Only worried about understanding/experience
dayBReview.notes: Managing game development while we continue to work through hardship

reportB.execution: I executed an idea that was integral for the story mode. In regards to the story, all four men (playable characters) have military backgrounds
reportB.tests: Our 2D side-scroller game shows the protagonist in the center at all times. That was a deliberate choice in programming.
reportB.handoff: All records are accessible within the Git
reportB.reflection: After creating the foundation of what our game is meant to be, the next step is to fine tune the visuals. Having better visuals creates a more captivating scene/environment which guides the user to consume the game at a higher volume than the average game.
